humanTitle: People reinstall the app to get back into their own work
whoItAffects: Android users in the United States, across three app versions.

build.proposition: A session that survives a crash, and a repair that is not a reinstall.
specifics: Keep the sign-in token out of whatever state the crash corrupts
Offer a reset that clears the broken state and keeps the account
Hold the second-factor screen when the authenticator takes focus
build.limitation: Reinstall-only faults usually live in stored state, which is the hardest thing to reproduce from a review.

start.proposition: A recovery layer that captures what an app was holding when it died.
specifics: Collects the crash with the account and session state attached
Aimed at teams whose chat tool is where the work actually happens
start.limitation: Crash reporting already runs inside these apps; the part missing is the part the person can see.

study.proposition: What does an app take with it when reinstalling is the fix?
specifics: Record what is lost each time: drafts, history, sign-in, settings
Compare the apps where reinstalling is the standard advice
study.limitation: People reinstall when nothing else has worked, so the sample is drawn only from the worst cases.

write.proposition: Turn it off and on again, except it is your job.
specifics: Follow one random sign-out through the reinstall it forces
Quote the reviewer locked out by the second step of sign-in
write.limitation: One build on one platform is a narrow story unless the same shape is found elsewhere.
